summary: The territory has not moved in 27 days and 60 commits (last src/ commit 0719673, 2026-07-28), while the map grew 24.98x faster than the code it describes over the project's whole life (git numstat: docs/ +358,674 lines vs src/ +14,355; on disk docs/ 33M vs src/ 752K). That ratio is a symptom; the mechanism is architectural and provable in four places. (1) All six of lane L0's binary gates grade the DOCUMENT -- cite integrity, judged-ness, convergence, sources opened, minimality, scorecard evidence (scripts/gauntlet/gateL0.py:9-14). Not one reads src/, a test, or a running build, so a lane can go 6/6 GREEN with the game byte-identical, and one has. (2) All 7 L0 workflow prompts hard-code 'This lane touches no source code' -- a prohibition strictly wider than GAUNTLET.md:236, which protects only src/core/Sim.ts and tests/duel-baseline.test.ts. The engine is FORBIDDEN from moving the territory, and the drift runs in the never-ship direction. (3) The map's only consumers are the map-makers: REBUILD_READINESS.md is referenced by 13 gauntlet scripts and 3 tests, and by exactly one file under src/ -- as a comment justifying an INFERRED placeholder (src/config/mobs.ts:69). Its accuracy is literally self-referential. (4) The decisive test of whether a better map yields a better territory: the answer is already on disk and was already ignored. reference/extracted/skilldata.xml (mtime Jul 25 18:27) states Chi Punch's cooldown as 5 and its chi cost as 2, verbatim; src/config/skills.ts ships chiPunch: 4960 graded CONTRACT off a 4.96s HUD readout, declares chi costs 'deliberately absent', and generalises the display artifact into an inference LAW ('.92/.96-ending pattern... the kickoff binds that pattern for INFERRED values too') from which two further cooldowns were invented. A perfectly accurate map of what we do not know sat on top of a file that knew it. The counterfactual is measured, not hypothetical: 159 lines of Python (scripts/anim/transcribeAnims.py, commit 741fd31) parsed the same reference/extracted/ directory and produced 854 lines of CONTRACT-grade data into src/config/ogAnims.ts -- the one time this project ran a transform instead of a swarm, the territory grew. The same parse run as a swarm produced 860K of docs/gauntlet/L0/index/*.json that only agents read. Verdict on the harder question: improving THIS map does not improve the territory later, because nothing routes map accuracy into src/ and one gate-clause explicitly forbids it. The map's accuracy is valuable mainly to the process that produces it.

findings.claim: All six of lane L0's binary gates grade properties of a document; none can detect whether the game changed, so a lane can close 6/6 GREEN with src/ byte-identical -- and the current one has, across 60 commits.

findings.proposed_change: Add L0-G TERRITORY DELTA to gateL0.py and one row to the GAUNTLET gate table: a lane closes only if it names at least one file under src/ or scripts/ that it created or changed, with the commit. A lane that legitimately produces none declares NO-TERRITORY in its header -- which makes the map-only lanes countable instead of invisible. Second-order: lanes will be tempted to make a token src/ edit to pass; the gate must require the file be cited by an A2 payload row, not merely touched. Rollback: delete the L0-G block from gateL0.py and the table row.

findings.proposed_change: DELETE the sentence 'This lane touches no source code.' from all 7 scripts/gauntlet/*.workflow.js prompt constants, leaving the accurate §4 line that names Sim.ts and duel-baseline.test.ts. Second-order: agents may now write to src/config, so the config-purity and byte-pin tests become the real guard -- they already exist and are chaos-planted. Rollback: git revert the one-line-per-file deletion. Word delta against standing rules is 0 because the deleted text lives in scripts, not in the rule docs -- which is exactly the D1 problem: the most restrictive rule in the system is not in any rule file.

findings.rule_targeted: the '.92/.96-ending pattern binds INFERRED values' inference rule in src/config/skills.ts (cited to the kickoff)
findings.proposed_change: DELETE the .92/.96 inference rule from src/config/skills.ts and from wherever the kickoff binds it. Replace the three cooldowns with the payload's own integers via a transcriber + byte-pin test, exactly as transcribeAnims.py/ogAnims.ts already does; chiPunch becomes 5000 with chi cost 2, both CONTRACT with an A2 cite. Real incident it prevents: two shipped numbers (smokeBomb 7960, stab 920) were generated by this rule and are almost certainly wrong. Second-order: the 4.96s frame measurement is not discarded but re-labelled -- it becomes evidence about the HUD's render offset, which the fidelity gate may want. Rollback: restore the comment block and the three literals from git.

findings.rule_targeted: docs/GAUNTLET.md §2 'THE RULE THAT OUTRANKS BOTH: A SCRIPT BEATS A SWARM'
findings.proposed_change: The rule is already correct and already written; it has no executable counterpart, which is defect D1's class. Bind it: any gauntlet index script that parses payload rows must emit the corresponding src/config/*.ts in the same run, with a byte-pin test, or the lane fails. Cheapest form is a test asserting that every file in docs/gauntlet/L0/index/ derived from a *.xml has a named consumer under src/. Second-order: this makes L0's index step slower and blocks the lane on schema decisions it currently defers -- which is the point, since deferring them is what froze the territory. Rollback: delete the test.

findings.proposed_change: DELETE the 12-system /100 scorecard from REBUILD_READINESS.md, and delete gate L0-F with it. Keep every banked claim, cite and overturn -- §6 of the kickoff protects that data and this does not touch it. The scorecard is the purest map artifact in the repo: a number expressing how much we know, which has never once routed to a line of code, and which was wrong by construction on 5 of 12 systems because its author never opened files that were on the same disk. Real incident: §2 scored skills-meters 33/100 with blocker 'every other skill's Chi cost + cooldown' while skilldata.xml held 81 chi values and 98 cooldowns (MT-3). Second-order: lane sequencing currently leans on the scores, so the replacement ordering signal must be named -- use count of unmined payload rows per system, which is countable and cannot be stale. Rollback: git revert the section and the L0-F block.

findings.proposed_change: Ratio ruling from this lens: the project is at roughly 96/4 map/territory by line churn and 100/0 for the last 27 days, against the Axe-Sharpening Philosophy's 10/90 for a late-stage project. Named next chop, in order and each closable in one session: (1) skilldata.xml -> src/config/skills.ts, all 75 skills with real chi and cooldown, byte-pinned -- transcribeAnims.py is the template and it is 159 lines; (2) itemdata.xml -> src/config/items.ts, 982 rows; (3) npcdata.xml -> src/config/npcs.ts, 495 rows. Second-order: L0's in-flight rewrite will need re-slicing once systems it scores become CONTRACT config -- that is a saving, not a cost.
